repo_notes.content: MAS-PromptBench is a benchmark for system-prompt optimization in multi-agent LLM systems. It measures the prompt-optimization gain (optimized minus seed-prompt score on the same examples) across 9 tasks, 5 workflow topologies (single, independent, sequential, centralized, decentralized) implemented in LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen and the OpenAI SDK, 3 communication protocols (freeform, semi_structured, structured_soft) and team sizes 2/4/8/10, using the GEPA and MIPRO optimizers. The hosted tutorial is at https://fm8995610-ops.github.io/MAS-PromptBench/docs/ and mirrors these pages.
repo_notes.author: Maintainers

repo_notes.content: Gotchas to state wherever relevant: (1) run every runner as a module from the repo root, e.g. python -m topologies.single.hotpotqa.langgraph_hotpotqa; the file-path form fails with ModuleNotFoundError because most runners import the topologies package before adding the repo root to sys.path. (2) gpqa/hotpotqa/math/lcb/apps runners take --batch and --out (without --out a batch only prints scores); bfcl and swe have no --batch flag and take --out-dir; toolhop and apibank take --out-dir; toolhop needs TOOLHOP_ALLOW_DATASET_EXEC=1. (3) The optimizers ignore VLLM_BASE_URL for task calls; set GEPA_TASK_ENDPOINTS / GEPA_REFL_ENDPOINT (MIPRO_* for MIPRO), TASK_MODEL and REFL_MODEL. (4) The GEPA/MIPRO pilots default to --n-agents 2 --n-rounds 1; pass --n-agents 4 --n-rounds 2 to optimize the same team the runners use. (5) Eval-ID exclusion (GEPA_EXCLUDE_REAL_EVAL_IDS) is on unless set to 0/false/no/off. (6) GEPA needs DSPy 3 (dspy.teleprompt.GEPA).
